title: tau explain --json output
description: Schema for the JSON `tau explain [--json]` prints on stdout. With a <code|type|key|doctor.<check>|TAU_*|client.<name>> query the output is a single entry object — an error entry for a code/type query, a config-key entry for a key query (including dotted keys.<provider> member paths), a doctor-check entry for a `doctor.<check>` or bare check-id query, an env-var entry for an exact TAU_* variable name, or a client entry for a `client.<name>` or bare client name/alias query; with no query it is a catalog object {"errors":[entry, ...],"config_keys":[key_entry, ...],"doctor_checks":[check_entry, ...],"env_vars":[env_entry, ...],"clients":[client_entry, ...]} holding every entry; under --list it is a topic-index object {"topics":{"errors":[{"code":N,"type":"T"}, ...],"config_keys":["<key>", ...],"doctor_checks":["doctor.<id>", ...],"env_vars":["TAU_*", ...],"clients":["client.<name>", ...]}} naming every resolvable query (error entries carry both addressable forms, code and type tag). Error entries describe one stable exit code: code doubles as the process exit status, type is the wire tag used in err envelopes, cause/hint are informational remediation text (may be reworded), docs is the guide link. Config-key entries mirror one row of the generated docs/config.md table: key is the config-file key, type its JSON type, constraints the constraint cell text, description the key's description, docs the config reference link. Doctor-check entries mirror one row of the generated check table in docs/troubleshooting.md: check is the `tau doctor` report row id, fails_when the condition that warns/fails, remediation the fix, docs the troubleshooting-section link. Env-var entries mirror one row of the generated docs/env.md table: env is the TAU_* variable name, section its doc grouping (tau | installer | external), consumers what reads it, summary what it does, docs the env reference link. Client entries mirror one row of the generated docs/compatibility.md matrix: client is the canonical `tau setup --client` name, transport how the editor reaches tau (acp | mcacp), wiring how setup installs the entry (direct | snippet), prereqs the setup prerequisites, setup the one-command wiring invocation, config_dir the detection directory, settings_path the config file that carries the entry (the settings file for direct clients, the snippet merge target for snippet clients), snippet_path the paste-ready fallback, bridge_path the shared mcacp config (mcacp transports only), verify the restart + in-editor step, doctor_check the `tau doctor` row id, docs the per-client guide link. New keys may be added (additive); existing keys keep their names and types.

code.description: Exit code this entry documents; also the process exit status when the error is raised.

type.description: Wire tag used in the err envelope's "type" field (e.g. "AuthFailed").

recoverable.description: Whether retrying the operation can succeed.

cause.description: One line naming when this error is raised; informational, may be reworded.

hint.description: Remediation hint; informational, may be reworded.

docs.description: Guide link for this error class.

key.description: Config-file key this entry documents — a flat key (e.g. "timeout_ms") or a dotted keys.<provider> member path (e.g. "keys.openai").

type.description: JSON type the config key accepts.

constraints.description: Constraint cell text identical to the generated docs/config.md Constraints column (enum members, ranges, non-empty, member-name rules; "—" when unconstrained); informational, may be reworded.

description.description: One line describing what the key controls; informational, may be reworded.

docs.description: Link to the generated config-key reference (docs/config.md).

check.description: Check id as it appears in the `tau doctor` report's "name" field (e.g. "tls_ca", "client_zed", "probe_openai_auth"); queried as `doctor.<check>` or bare.

fails_when.description: The condition that makes the check warn or fail — the same cell text the generated docs/troubleshooting.md check table renders; informational, may be reworded.

remediation.description: The fix that resolves the check — flag, env var, or command; informational, may be reworded.

docs.description: Link to the doctor-checks section of docs/troubleshooting.md.

env.description: TAU_* environment variable name as it appears in the generated docs/env.md catalog (e.g. "TAU_ENDPOINT", "TAU_VERSION"); queried by exact (uppercase) name.

section.description: docs/env.md grouping — "tau" for variables the tau binary reads, "installer" for install.sh/install.ps1-only variables, "external" for companion tooling (a2a-spawn, scripts/smoke.sh).

consumers.description: What reads the variable — the same cell text the generated docs/env.md Consumed-by column renders; informational, may be reworded.

summary.description: One line describing what the variable controls — the generated docs/env.md Purpose cell; informational, may be reworded.

docs.description: Link to the generated env-var reference (docs/env.md).

client.description: Canonical `tau setup --client` name (e.g. "zed", "claude-desktop"); queried as `client.<name>` or bare — `--client` aliases (`code`, `claude`, `roo`, `kilo`, `gemini-cli`, `amazon-q`, `codex-cli`) resolve too.

transport.description: How the editor reaches tau — "acp" spawns `tau acp serve` directly; "mcacp" goes through the mcacp MCP→ACP bridge.

wiring.description: How `tau setup --client` installs the entry — "direct" splices the settings file; "snippet" writes a paste-ready fragment under ~/.config/tau/snippets/ for a config format it can't splice (Lua/elisp/YAML/TOML).

prereqs.description: Setup prerequisites — mirrors the ## Prerequisites section of the per-client guide; informational, may be reworded.

config_dir.description: The directory whose existence marks the client installed (detection only — never written).

settings_path.description: The config file that carries the agent/server entry — the settings file setup splices (direct clients) or the native file the snippet merges into (snippet clients).

snippet_path.description: Where the paste-ready fallback snippet lands (~/.config/tau/snippets/).

bridge_path.description: Present only for transport "mcacp" — the shared mcacp bridge config (~/.config/mcacp/mcacp.json).

verify.description: The restart + in-editor step that finishes the integration — mirrors the ## In-editor finish row of docs/compatibility.md; informational, may be reworded.

doctor_check.description: The `tau doctor` row id that verifies the wiring — also resolvable via `tau explain doctor.<id>`.

docs.description: Link to the per-client setup guide (docs/clients/<name>.md).

errors.description: Every entry in the stable error catalog, ordered by exit code.

config_keys.description: Every resolvable config key — each generated docs/config.md key row plus each keys.<provider> member path.

doctor_checks.description: Every resolvable `tau doctor` check id — each row of the generated docs/troubleshooting.md check table.

env_vars.description: Every resolvable TAU_* environment variable — each row of the generated docs/env.md tables (tau binary, installers, and companion tooling sections).

clients.description: Every supported `tau setup --client` editor client — each row of the generated docs/compatibility.md matrix.

code.description: Exit code — `tau explain <code>` resolves the entry.

type.description: Wire tag — `tau explain <type>` resolves the same entry (case-insensitive).

errors.description: Every catalog error topic, ordered by exit code; each carries both addressable forms.

config_keys.description: Every resolvable config-key name — flat keys, keys.<provider> member paths, and deprecated spellings.

doctor_checks.description: Every resolvable doctor check in the canonical `doctor.<id>` spelling (bare ids resolve too unless they collide with a config key).

env_vars.description: Every resolvable TAU_* environment variable name.

clients.description: Every supported editor client in the canonical `client.<name>` spelling (bare names and --client aliases resolve too).

examples.cause: the provider rejected the API key, or no key was found anywhere in the resolution chain
examples.hint: provide an API key via --api-key, the provider env var, config.json, or TAU_API_KEY

examples.fails_when: CURL_CA_BUNDLE/SSL_CERT_FILE points at a missing or non-file path, or an SSL_CERT_DIR entry is missing (fail — every HTTPS request would error); a configured proxy with no custom CA bundle warns — the corporate TLS-intercept case (runs under --offline)
examples.remediation: set CURL_CA_BUNDLE (or SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR) to your organization's PEM bundle, or fix/remove the missing path

examples.summary: Overrides the provider's endpoint URL (works for chat and `tau acp`). Useful for proxies, gateways, and local OpenAI-compatible servers.

examples.prereqs: tau installed and configured — `tau doctor` reports an ok provider and API key
examples.verify: open the Agent Panel, click +, and pick tau

errors.cause: a named resource is missing — the message identifies the file, skill, or session
errors.hint: the message names what was not found — check the name/path and retry

config_keys.description: Active provider name — selects the API endpoint and default model. TAU_ENDPOINT overrides the endpoint.

doctor_checks.fails_when: CURL_CA_BUNDLE/SSL_CERT_FILE points at a missing or non-file path, or an SSL_CERT_DIR entry is missing (fail — every HTTPS request would error); a configured proxy with no custom CA bundle warns — the corporate TLS-intercept case (runs under --offline)
doctor_checks.remediation: set CURL_CA_BUNDLE (or SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR) to your organization's PEM bundle, or fix/remove the missing path

env_vars.summary: Overrides the provider's endpoint URL (works for chat and `tau acp`). Useful for proxies, gateways, and local OpenAI-compatible servers.

clients.prereqs: tau installed and configured — `tau doctor` reports an ok provider and API key
clients.verify: open the Agent Panel, click +, and pick tau
